title: Entergy and NOABJ honor journalism trailblazers and support emerging storytellers
summary: Entergy proudly served as presenting sponsor of the New Orleans Association of Black Journalists’ 4th Annual Jazz Brunch and Silent Auction, reinforcing our commitment to education and community…
body_markdown:
Entergy proudly served as presenting sponsor of the New Orleans Association of Black Journalists’ 4th Annual Jazz Brunch and Silent Auction, reinforcing our commitment to education and community investment. The event brought together journalists, media professionals, academia and community leaders to honor industry trailblazers and support the next generation of journalists.


“Journalism plays an important role in keeping our communities informed, connected and engaged,” said Deanna Rodriguez, president and CEO of Entergy New Orleans. “We are proud to partner with NOABJ to honor industry leaders and invest in the next generation of communications professionals.”


Rodriguez along with Herman Lee, utility foreman, presented the 2026 Legacy Awards to Terry Baquet, Jinx Broussard, Hal Clark and Tod Smith, recognizing their distinguished careers and enduring contributions to journalism.


Entergy also presented the 2026 Unsung Hero Award to Dominic Martin, a longtime WDSU-TV photojournalist. The award recognizes behind-the-scenes professionals whose dedication and contributions are instrumental to telling the stories that inform and connect our communities.


A highlight of the event was the presentation of four $2,500 scholarships, partially funded by Entergy’s sponsorship of the event, to aspiring journalists: Dessadra Tezeno of Loyola University New Orleans, Trent Granberry of Nicholls State University, Raygan Irvin of Xavier University of Louisiana and Hannah Glenn of Louisiana State University.


Our partnership with NOABJ reflects Entergy’s broader commitment to expanding educational opportunities, including the company’s Power of Prosperity $20 million investment in historically Black colleges and universities.


By investing in education and supporting organizations like NOABJ, we’re helping cultivate diverse voices, create pathways to meaningful careers and strengthen the communities we proudly call home.
